title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Pet grooming
audience: Groomers who want repeat bookings and referrals from owners they have already groomed, including referrals from clinics and pet businesses.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask once the owner is happy with the result
instruction.body: The best time to ask for a review or referral is after the owner has seen the result and collected the animal, or after payment. Ask in one sentence, name the step you want (a review, or the name of one person who might want a groom), and make it easy to say no. Record what you asked and the reply. One experiment found that a late reminder brought in more reviews than an immediate one, but it was a single study and not an Australian one (Baylor Keller Center, 1 June 2024). Google provides a review link or QR code you can share. Never write reviews for owners, invent them, or ask only the owners you expect to be happy: a vendor source describes that as review gating, which Google treats as a violation (Podium, 2 May 2022). Google also bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews (Google Business Profile Help, no date shown), and the ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (ACCC, 15 July 2026).

instruction.heading: Offer the next groom before the owner leaves
instruction.body: Propose the next appointment with a date, based on the coat and the service, and write it down with the scope and the price approach. Confirm the owner agrees before you change the diary. The research found no Australian source on rebooking intervals or repeat-visit rates for groomers, so any interval you choose is your own working choice and not a benchmark. A six-weekly cycle is only an example to test. If the offer goes by email or text, check the electronic message rules first (ACMA, no date shown).

instruction.heading: Check in at the interval that suits the coat
instruction.body: Schedule a check-in around the next due date for the coat. A short message asks whether the coat and skin are still in good shape, whether anything has changed, and whether the owner wants the next groom booked. A message that promotes a service can be commercial even when it is framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, 9 November 2023), so check it before sending.

instruction.heading: Plan re-contact before busy periods
instruction.body: Plan short messages before the periods you can see in your own bookings. No Australian source for seasonal or holiday demand for grooming was found, so set the dates from your own history. Offer the slots you can deliver, on written terms, with a clear way to opt out. ACMA says an unsubscribe must be honoured within five working days (ACMA, no date shown), so record each opt-out as soon as you receive it.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: Decide the reward, such as a credit on the next groom, and write down the payment condition, which is normally that the referred owner completes a paid groom. Give the referrer a copy. In seven studies, stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals (Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research, 2023). A referral from a vet clinic or pet shop should be written as a business arrangement, and check the clinic's own rules first. The research found no Australian figure for how often clinics refer clients. Get the referred owner's consent before any message is sent to them (Clayton Utz, 2017; an older source). The tax and contract effect of rewards is UNCONFIRMED, so check any cash reward with an adviser.

procedure: After each groom is collected and paid, make one review or referral request and record the request and the reply.
Write the next-groom offer with a date, the scope and the price approach, and confirm it with the owner.
Schedule the check-in around the next due date for the coat, and send it under the electronic message rules.
Plan re-contact dates from your own bookings, and exclude anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward and its payment condition before the first referral.
When a referred owner completes a paid groom, apply the reward and record the outcome.

workedExamples.situation: A receptionist at a local veterinary clinic says she will recommend the groomer to clients who ask about grooming. The groomer would like to offer the clinic a credit on his services for each client who books and completes a paid groom.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the groomer write down before any client is referred, and what should he avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: He writes the credit, the condition (the referred client completes a paid groom), when the credit is applied, and how referrals are recorded, and gives the clinic a copy. He checks the clinic's own rules on payments for referrals before he starts. He does not contact any client the clinic gives him until the client agrees to be contacted, and he does not promise a reward he has not written down. If he is unsure of the tax or contract effect of a credit, he checks with an adviser. A referral does not extend his licence, registration or insurance, so he accepts only the work they cover, in the place where he works.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the groom date, the next due date and the review or referral request made
Next-groom offer template with date, scope and price approach
Calendar of re-contact dates built from your own bookings
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any groom follows your own safety checklist

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the owner has seen the result
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after the owner has seen the result and collected the animal, or at payment.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing an owner's name, photo or review, or an animal's details, without consent
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting an owner who asked not to hear from you
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list, honour it at once, and keep messages factual and optional.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing an owner's name, photo, review or an animal's details needs the owner's consent for that use. Do not write reviews for an owner or invent them. Owner details may be personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) if it applies to your business. Check the OAIC small business guidance to see whether it applies.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own incentive rules. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews, and the ACCC says incentives must be disclosed. Check each platform's rules, and any clinic's rules, before you offer a reward.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). The Spam Act text was not read for this research, so check it before sending.

A referral does not extend the licence, registration or insurance of the groomer. Accept only the work they cover, in the state or territory where the work is done. Victorian grooming rules are UNRESOLVED.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after the owner has seen the result or paid, and includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-groom offer is written, dated and confirmed by the owner before the diary changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log, with the date and the reply
Next-groom offers with the date, scope, interval and owner confirmation
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the owner has seen the result, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next groom in writing, with a date, before the owner leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask an owner for a review or referral?
options: Before the groom starts, so the owner feels committed
After the owner has seen the result and collected the animal
Only when the owner has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: An owner wants to post a review with her name and a photo of her dog. What do you need?
options: Her consent for the name and photo you plan to publish
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred owner books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the payment condition stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say to propose the next groom?
options: At the end of each groom, with a date

sourceReferences: Baylor Keller Center, 'Wait Just a Minute', https://kellercenter.hankamer.baylor.edu/news/story/2024/wait-just-minute-when-ask-online-reviews, 1 June 2024 (metadata says 13 May 2024). One experiment only.
ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026.
Google Business Profile Help, review links and the rule on rewards, https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122?hl=en-GB, no date shown.
Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; the Google position was not checked against Google's own policy.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Stating the referrer reward in the invitation; no figures used.
Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017. Older than 2022.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023.
ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown; read 2026-11-03 or 2026-11-04 per the research file.
Gap: no Australian data on groomer rebooking or referral rates was found. The Baylor figure is from one experiment and is not an Australian rate.
Gap: no business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found; the tax and contract effect of rewards is UNCONFIRMED.
Gap: no Australian data on how often vet clinics or pet shops refer clients was found.

officialReferences.title: ACMA, Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: Recorded from the team4 research files (read 2026-11-03 or 2026-11-04), not reopened: marketing messages need consent, and consent should be recorded; each message identifies the sender, and its unsubscribe works for 30 days and is honoured within five working days. Does not mention one-to-one messages.
